chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who shook the hand of a Magian man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash his hand and he does not have to perform ablution.'

key_terms.مَجُوسِيّاً: Magian (Zoroastrian), a specific group of People of the Book in Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.وَلَا يَتَوَضَّأُ: And he does not perform ablution (wudu)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing hands after shaking hands with a Magian?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *ghusl* versus *wudu* in the context of social interaction with *Ahl al-Kitab*, specifically Zoroastrians recognized as People of the Book in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the distinction between major ritual impurity (*janabah*) and minor impurity (*hadath*), indicating that physical contact alone does not necessitate the full ablution required for prayer, but rather a simple washing to remove physical residue or minor impurity. This ruling underscores the practical ease of maintaining ritual purity during daily interactions with non-Muslims in Islamic society.
